record.label: Inverse distance from three comparisons and a Bernstein lookup
record.statement: The solution partitions the range of squared distances $r^2$ into intervals. On each interval a cubic Bernstein polynomial with four precomputed coefficients approximates $1/r$. Three comparisons determine which coefficient to look up.
record.boundary: If $p=\tilde{r}^2$ is the rescaled position in an interval, the probability of exactly one success in three independent Bernoulli trials is $3p(1-p)^2$, the Bernstein weight of $w_1$. The other counts give the weights of $w_0$, $w_2$ and $w_3$. Lean bounds the error of the implemented lookup expectation for realizable squared distances $r^2$ with $r^2\not\equiv7\pmod 8$, using saturation thresholds of 1 and 8.
